QF.id: Analysis of Equity and Debt Instruments_12

question.text: Regarding Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), which statement correctly describes the tax treatment of income earned by the fund?

answer.text: All three categories (I, II, III) enjoy complete pass-through status for all types of income
Category III AIFs enjoy pass-through for capital gains but not for business income

Category I and II AIFs have pass-through for income other than business income; business income is taxed at the fund level at the rate applicable to the fund entity. Category III has no pass-through and is taxed at the fund level as the relevant normal entity (subject to specified-fund concessions where applicable).
Category I AIFs have pass-through status, but Category II and III do not

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Level 2 workbook (pages 283-287), Category I and II AIFs enjoy pass-through status for income other than business income; that pass-through income is taxed in the hands of investors. Business income earned by Cat I/II is taxed at the fund level at the rate applicable to the fund entity - that is, at company / firm rates where applicable, and at Maximum Marginal Rate (MMR) where the AIF is set up as a trust or other body corporate. Category III AIFs have no pass-through; the AIF itself is taxed as the relevant normal entity, with specified-fund concessions where applicable. The Trap: Option A overstates pass-through (it is not 'complete' and does not apply to Cat III). Option B reverses the Cat III treatment. Option D wrongly restricts pass-through to Cat I only. A blanket 'all income at MMR' claim is also incorrect because the fund-level rate depends on the fund's legal form. Note: Cat III AIFs (typically hedge funds) generally face fund-level taxation, which can be a meaningful headwind for investors in lower brackets. Cat I/II structures preserve pass-through for non-business income, which is a key tax-neutrality feature.
